<description>
As discussed in #36403, one of the issues with current rebroadcast behavior is that the rebroadcast begins an unconditional relay of a transaction to peers. While this is broadcast is limited to peers that have not previously been inv'd the transaction, there is still a privacy leak in this double relay of a transaction, especially so for transactions that are still in nodes' mempools.

This PR changes the rebroadcast to only rebroadcast transactions if the transaction was not already present in our mempool. This provides some additional privacy while retaining intended rebroadcast behavior as transactions that have likely fallen out of nodes' mempools are the ones that actually need to be rebroadcast.

The wallet rebroadcast tests are additionally refactored for isolation so that their behaviors can still be tested after this change. Additionally, a test for the loading resubmission was added, as well as a test for the new behavior.
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6395009208 comment by fametrano (contributor):
After a restart, this branch does not announce a wallet transaction that peers already received while our own mempool keeps it, so the answer to murch's question is yes.

I built 4dbd27f37b and its base f739c7876b and ran a regtest script that connects a fresh P2PInterface peer, moves mocktime 36 hours ahead so that MaybeResendWalletTxs runs, and sends an unrelated transaction as a barrier. A wallet transaction still in the mempool is announced on base and not on the branch, as intended. One that expired and was accepted again is announced on both. One rejected as non-final is announced on neither.

With -persistmempool=0, the load-time resubmission puts the transaction back without broadcast. With mempool.dat, it comes back already out of the unbroadcast set, because a peer requested it before shutdown. The branch announced nothing in either case, and with -persistmempool=0 nothing over two periodic resubmissions and six ReattemptInitialBroadcast windows; base announced it at each resubmission. The same holds whenever our mempool keeps a transaction that peers dropped, until it expires from our mempool (two weeks by default). A node offline for days now takes its own mempool as a proxy for everyone else's. test_resubmit_on_load stops before the first periodic resubmission; extending it would pin whichever behaviour is intended.

Smaller: the comment above ResubmitWalletTransactions still names MEMPOOL_AND_BROADCAST_TO_ALL for the periodic path, and "resubmit N unconfirmed transactions" now counts transactions not relayed. I can share the script as a gist.
</new_statements>
